title: Rising memory costs may push mobile prices up 30%, could trigger second-hand device market: Jefferies
snippet: Rising memory costs, driven by growing demand from the artificial intelligence industry, could push prices of low-end smartphones up by around 30 per cent and force consumers to delay fresh purchases or opt for second-hand devices, according to a report by Jefferies.

title: What is Hangang? South Korea unveils a $276 million supercomputer with 614.7 petaflops of computing power
snippet: South Korea has launched Hangang, a $276 million national supercomputer equipped with 8,496 Nvidia GPUs and 614.7 petaflops of computing power. Designed to accelerate AI and scientific research, the system is expected to rank among the world's top 10 supercomputers.

title: Sony PS5 trade-in offer: US gamers can get up to $400 for old consoles ahead of GTA 6 launch; check details
snippet: Sony is offering US gamers up to $400 in cash for trading in their old PlayStation 5 consoles through a partnership with refurbished electronics marketplace Back Market, according to TweakTown. The offer could help players upgrade to the $899.99 PS5 Pro ahead of the much-anticipated GTA 6 launch.

title: AI moves beyond recommendations to reshape entire shopping experience on e-commerce apps: Report

title: Realme 17T 5G live images reveal redesigned camera module and slimmer bezels ahead of launch

title: 87% of organisations face threat-related incidents, preparedness gaps persist: McKinsey
snippet: Around 87 per cent of organisations experienced at least one threat-related incident in the 24 months preceding a survey, but many remain inadequately prepared to deal with risks beyond conventional cybersecurity, according to a report by McKinsey & Company.

title: Figma banking on AI credits, in-house model to lift margins
snippet: Figma is leaning on cashing in on its AI features through credits and using its first-party model to power tasks on its design software platform to bolster its margins, finance chief Praveer Melwani told Reuters on Wednesday.

title: Australia data centre inquiry finds inadequate checks, stops short of moratorium
snippet: An inquiry into data centres by Australia's most populous state found approvals failed to consider the cumulative effect on resources and infrastructure but stopped short of calling for a moratorium, prompting a blistering rebuke from its chair.

title: OpenAI, ready to IPO in 2027, now counts majority of sales from enterprises, Greg Brockman says
